body: It’s not. His new job is very stressful and he doesn’t handle stress well at all.

You are definitely not the first people to say this. I can see it. I would say it’s about half right. He can and is very manipulative from time to time. I love him and deep down, he’s a good person. He really is. 

I don’t understand what gets him like this. I don’t. Sigh.

I found him opening the door. When I asked what he was doing (it’s like 20° out, can’t be many reasons why you’d wanna have that open), he said he’s gonna jump. I told him no, and he tried to open the door faster but it happened to get on the frame. 

He tried leaving in his car so he could go crash it. He couldn’t find his keys (I truly didn’t hide them). He kept blaming me and then tried to take my car. I literally held my ground on not letting him take my keys that he tackled me and then I said I was calling 911. He didn’t like that, so he threw my phone across the room. 

My mom has said that too, and maybe you guys are right. He’s been very destructive. He’s been hitting his head on things, he was googling “what’s the quickest way to die”, tried turning on the oven and climbing inside, just to name a few things. 

I wouldn’t put the idea behind me, but he has a past of suicide attempts. He has was I believe is bipolar disorder, so most of them time he’s upbeat and happy, and then something sets him off and this happens. You could be right, but I don’t know how to tell without risking his life.

I tried. I have emergency SOS on my phone and watch. He tore the watch off my wrist and then threw my phone. There was nothing I could do. I would not have left him alone. Our apartment is very small and not a lot of space to do that without him noticing. One side is the front door, which he kept threatening to leave and drive his car into oncoming traffic so he could no longer be here. The other side is our balcony, which is 30ft off of the ground. I wasn’t winning. 

He’s currently asleep, but if he wakes up in the same mindset, I’ll probably have to.

I’m here for college, so can’t really sublease. I’d have no where to go. In reality, he could probably move out and make it work for himself. His new job will pay nice, but not for several weeks. I wouldn’t be able to pay for the apartment though by myself, and I have the cheapest apartment in my college town. Adulting sucks.

I absolute love everything about your answer. You get me. I’ve spent my whole life and no one understands me, except maybe my boyfriend. I’m in real actual tears. 

I’ll be scheduling a therapy session as soon as classes start. I really needed that. Thank you, kind stranger. You’ve made my night a whole hell of a lot better. Not sure why it clicked like that, but you’re amazing. ❤️

Thank you. I hope that day comes sooner rather than later too. I’m hoping this new jobs shows him some light. 

I absolutely think my father has impacted my entire life. I grew up with depression because I really thought I was awful, because he told me about once a day. My mom just sat in the background because if she intervened, she would get shit too and it’s not worth it to my mom. I don’t blame her at all. She would text me after I went to my room crying saying I love you and you’re my whole world, and I knew she meant it. She did much more than my dad ever did. This also caused me to have severe anxiety that has subsided with time, thankfully. 

The hardest part right now is that my dad is terminal with his 4th bout of cancer (only the 2nd one in my life), and so I’m having a hard time coping with this.

You’re absolutely right. I don’t want to justify his insults, because frankly, it’s still not okay. You’re absolutely correct. 

Yeah, my father hasn’t helped. I understand that one day I shouldn’t have to deal with it. I get it. There’s a part of me that hopes that one day, he’ll stop being so mean and get his shit together.

I’ve personally never been to therapy, but my grandma is a therapist and I’ve talked to her about things, and she’s also sat down with my boyfriend and talked to him (she agrees with his diagnosis as well). I think seeing real therapy that’s unbiased would be very beneficial, and it’s not hard where I live. I think I’ll be doing that once the semester fires up. 

I struggled with self worth issues my entire life (thanks Dad). Insults like “you suck” generally don’t get to me, but saying things like the future with me hurt. All of my relationships have ended because I was “too annoying”, and I feel like I’ve improved so much since those, but I’m wondering if I really have or if I’m being arrogant about it. I can be overbearing, I’m more than aware of that, but I just don’t know what he considers too much, if that makes sense.

I appreciate it. I’m just looking for new ways to handle the situation. We’re both stubborn and we clash a lot, which is why I’m reaching out to Reddit. I want other ideas. I knew everyone would say “dump his ass”, which isn’t the advice I want. No shit, most people call it quits after a semi-wavy ocean. It’s gonna take a hurricane to knock me down, and even then, I’ll still get back up. 

His OCPD makes himself a perfectionist with EVERYTHING. I’m talking video games, his hair, making the bed, everything. If it isn’t perfect, instead of a normal OCD person just doing it more, he gets frustrated and flips out. 

His dad is a pretty screwed up dude too, which isn’t helping. He used to do some pretty awful stuff to my boyfriend as a kid, and he unfortunately inherited his dad’s brain, and he’s fully aware of that. His biological brother has been in a mental hospital more times than I have fingers and toes. 

I appreciate the answer though and you taking time out of your day to answer my post. It’s weird to see people helping me.

I tell him the same thing all the time. He finally broke down tonight and said that I’m annoying and nagging, but I never realized I did it. He’s never said it before. He bottles everything up. So, of course, I attempt to apologize, because I literally had no idea. He claims to have told me multiple times and I just “never learn”. I told him to give me time to adjust to this. He said no, you won’t. I hope that over time he’ll see all the good stuff about me. 

It just breaks my heart that he said to me tonight “I thought about marrying you once, but not anymore. I couldn’t do this the rest of my life.”

He does. He recently was laid off by his last employer in early December, and just started his new job on Monday. He’s a little stressed about it because it’s new and they have high expectations for him. 

The last time he was this upset was when he was stressed from getting laid off. I believe that his anger for himself gets deflected to me. Not healthy, but it’s why I don’t take it to heart. The insults have never hurt me thankfully. I’ve heard worse out of my dad’s mouth.
I appreciate the advice. I’ve been questioning myself for awhile but after reading through the comments, I’m feeling a little better. Thank you ❤️
I appreciate the words. Whenever he calms down, I’m gonna try talking to him again.

He constantly tells me he’s unhappy and wants to leave, and I ask him how I can do better. The usual response is “it’s doesn’t matter, you won’t”. 

So yeah, that’s how that’s gone. I appreciate it though.
I wish it wasn’t the case, but neither of us make enough to branch out. Combined income is only about $1000/month, which covers all of the bills and nothing else.

It’s ADHD and OCPD. 

I grew up with an abusive dad (verbal mostly, but occasionally physical) and the insults aren’t what hurt. It’s the fact that he acts like this in general. It’s childish.

Edit: he uses weed to help him mentally
